newsitem.title: CHINA: China president urges U.S. to grant permanent MFN.
newsitem.headline: China president urges U.S. to grant permanent MFN.

text.p: President Jiang Zemin has called on the United States to be "sensible" and grant China permanent Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trade status, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

The United States should abandon its annual review of China's MFN status, the low-tariff treatment Washington accords most of its trading partners, Xinhua quoted Jiang as saying in an interview with a French newspaper.
"I hope U.S. leaders will adopt a sensible attitude and solve the MFN question once and for all," Jiang said.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said last month that China would likely win permanent MFN status if it were accepted into the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

Talks on China's entry into the WTO have been stalled, with Beijing demanding it should join the trade body under the easier terms granted developing nations and the United States and other countries insisting on tougher conditions.
"The U.S. side should also give up all forms of discriminative policies in trade with China in order to ensure a smooth development of economic and trade relations," Jiang said.

The U.S. and China went to the brink of a multi-billion dollar trade war in June after Washington threatened Beijing with huge tariffs in retaliation for the widespread violations of intellectual property rights in China.
"No doubt, good bilateral relations are conducive to the development of economic relations and trade and to expanded business in China," Jiang said.
